verdicts.claim: Checkpointing transfers committed page changes from the WAL into the main database. A WAL transaction can commit before those ch
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'a COMMIT can happen without ever writing to the original database' and 'Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a checkpoint'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpoints copy as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and never invoke the busy handl
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode' and 'might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers'

verdicts.claim: FULL checkpoint mode waits, subject to busy handling, for the writer to finish and readers to use the latest snapshot, then
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'blocks (invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot... syncs the database file'; c3ref: 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'

verdicts.claim: RESTART performs FULL checkpointing and additionally waits for readers to finish using the WAL. Successful completion ensu
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'blocks... until all readers are finished with the log file. This ensures that the next client to write to the database file restarts the log file from the beginning'; Fly: RESTART = 'restart but don't truncate WAL'

verdicts.claim: SQLite documents a default automatic checkpoint threshold of 1000 WAL pages, overridable at compile time. PRAGMA wal_autoch
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off... All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE... interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE performs the RESTART checkpoint procedure and additionally truncates the WAL file to zero bytes before returning
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'; pragma.html lists PRAGMA schema.wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)

verdicts.claim: For a single WAL database, PRAGMA main.wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) returns a busy indicator, the WAL frame count, and the check
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns' (busy flag, pages written to WAL, pages moved back into database); c3ref pnLog/pnCkpt

verdicts.claim: FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE checkpoint requests can return SQLITE_BUSY instead of completing. The SQL wal_checkpoint pragma
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'will be 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked from completing... 1 if the equivalent call would have returned SQLITE_BUSY'

verdicts.claim: Long-lived or overlapping read transactions that still need WAL content can limit checkpoint progress or prevent log reuse
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'

verdicts.claim: Checkpointing and WAL reuse do not normally shrink the physical WAL file: SQLite can overwrite it from the beginning. A ret
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.'
